title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes management.

HPI
Pt is a 73 y.o. female presenting for routine f/u of T2DM. Pt reports stable status and denies any acute concerns. She has been managed on a combination of insulin and an oral hypoglycemic for several years. She reports adherence to current regimen and denies any recent issues with glucose monitoring.

Medication List
- Insulin and metformin daily.

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 128/78, HR 72, RR 16, Temp 98.6 F.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Resp: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: Intact, no signs of infection.
Neuro: Grossly intact, WNL.

Assessment
1. T2DM without complications.

Plan
- Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin.
- Pt to continue monitoring blood glucose levels.
- F/u in 3 months for routine labs and management.

Electronically signed,
M. Okafor, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
